entities.name: PMID:25084165
observations: Prospective cohort of 2,131 active healthy working adults (34% women) assessed at three time points over 3.7 years.
Increase in insomnia symptoms from T1 to T2 predicted new back pain at T3 after adjustment for socioeconomic variables, self-reported health, lifestyle behaviors, and anthropometrics.
Adjusted odds ratio was 1.40 (95% CI 1.10–1.71); the study found no support for back pain predicting later increases in insomnia symptoms.

entities.name: Insomnia predicts back pain
observations: In employed healthy adults, increased insomnia symptoms over the first interval were associated with 1.40-fold higher odds of new back pain at the later assessment (adjusted OR 1.40, 95% CI 1.10–1.71).
The longitudinal ordering supports prediction, but the observational design does not establish causation.
